absent: Locking, concurrency and calling context rules for link settings and netlink handling.
Netlink command numbers, dispatch, reply construction and error codes beyond attribute lists.
Transition triggers and timing for autonegotiation, master slave, rate matching and power sourcing events.
Meanings of MDIO support bits, link mode mask bit assignments, lane counts and signal quality ranges.
Memory ownership and lifetime for variable length mask arrays and string sets.
Remainder of energy efficient Ethernet attributes and later definitions beyond the truncated fragment.
Reset execution semantics, ordering, duration and failure reporting.

findings.text: The interface provides a family of advertised capability aliases that each resolve through a legacy link mode mask helper. The family spans classic twisted pair rates in half and full duplex, autonegotiation, common media and connector kinds, ten gigabit twisted pair, pause and asymmetric pause, a twenty five hundred variant, backplane, single and multi lane backplane forms, forward error correction, and higher twenty to fifty six gigabit KR CR SR LR groups plus an MLD variant. Each member denotes a bit position in the historic advertisement word.
Lower link rates use decimal megabit constants with values 10, 100, 1000, 2500, 5000, 10000, 14000, 20000 and 25000. They form an ascending scale for the speed field.
Higher link rates continue the same decimal megabit scale with values 40000, 50000, 56000, 80000, 100000, 200000, 400000, 800000 and 1600000. A separate sentinel of negative one means unknown rate.

A speed word is accepted when it is numerically no larger than the maximum signed kernel integer, or when it equals the unknown sentinel reinterpreted as unsigned. All larger unsigned values are rejected, so the valid set is the full non negative signed range plus one wrapped sentinel.
Duplex is a single byte where half duplex is 0x00, full duplex is 0x01 and unknown is 0xff. No other duplex code is defined.
Duplex validity is decided by a tiny side effect free predicate that returns true only for the half, full and unknown codes and false for any other byte value.

Master slave configuration is a small integer from zero to five meaning unsupported, unknown, preferred master, preferred slave, forced master and forced slave in order. The encoding is a plain integer, not a bitmask.

The observed master slave role is one of five mutually exclusive conditions numbered zero to four for unsupported, unknown, master, slave and error. Error is distinct from unknown, and master and slave are the two successful negotiated outcomes. The fragments define the vocabulary only and show no transition events or timing.
Rate matching mode is a small integer where none is 0, pause based is 1, carrier sense based is 2 and open loop is 3. Only these four values are defined.

Port and connector kind is a byte where twisted pair is 0x00, attachment unit is 0x01, media independent is 0x02, fibre is 0x03, coaxial is 0x04 and direct attach is 0x05, with none as 0xef and other as 0xff. The low six values are sequential while the two specials are isolated high patterns.

Transceiver location is 0x00 for internal where PHY and MAC share a package and 0x01 for external where they are separate, plus reserved codes 0x02, 0x03 and 0x04. Autonegotiation is 0x00 for off and 0x01 for on. Twisted pair crossover is 0x00 for invalid or unknown, 0x01 for straight, 0x02 for crossed and 0x03 for automatic, where automatic applies to control only.

Wake on LAN causes are single bits with physical activity at shift zero, unicast at one, multicast at two, broadcast at three, address resolution at four, magic packet at five, secured magic at six and filter at seven. Together they occupy the low byte.

The secured magic wake bit has effect only when the plain magic packet bit is also set, and the total number of defined wake modes is eight. Code must not interpret the secured bit alone as an independent wake source.

Receive hash transformation provides a symmetric exclusive or option at shift zero and a symmetric inclusive or with exclusive or option at shift one, plus a dedicated no change code of 0xff. The no change value is a full byte sentinel rather than a bit combination.

Flow classification uses values 0x01 to 0x03 for version four TCP UDP SCTP for hash or specification, with 0x04 for combined security as hash only. Values 0x05 to 0x07 mirror the transports for version six for hash or specification, with 0x08 for combined security as hash only. Values 0x09 to 0x0c separate authentication and ESP for both IP versions for hash or specification. Value 0x0d is version four user flow with an alias for generic IP user flow, and 0x0e is version six user flow, both specification only, with 0x0f unused. Values 0x10 and 0x11 are raw version four and six hash only, 0x12 is Ethernet hash or specification, and 0x13 through 0x1e are tunnelling user control endpoint and session container uplink downlink forms all hash only. A trailing count ends the enumeration.

Extension flags occupy high bits of a 32 bit word with generic extension at 0x80000000, MAC extension at 0x40000000 and receive side scaling at 0x20000000. Hash inputs use shift one for layer two destination, two for VLAN, three for protocol, four for IP source, five for IP destination, six and seven for the two transport byte pairs, eight for tunnel identifier and nine for version six flow label, with discard at shift thirty one. Drop uses all 64 bits set while wake uses all but the lowest bit. Classifier locations use a special flag at 0x80000000 with any as 0xffffffff, first as 0xfffffffe and last as 0xfffffffd.

Pluggable module standards use type identifiers one through four for small form factor specifications, with data lengths of 256, 512, 256 and 256 respectively in identifier order. Two extended maximum lengths of 640 apply to the newer 8636 and 8436 families.

Reset selection uses low bits zero through eight for management, interrupt, DMA, filter, offload, MAC, PHY, shared RAM and application processor. A dedicated mask covers the low sixteen bits and an all mask sets all thirty two bits, while shared components are addressed by shifting a dedicated bit left by sixteen.

The link settings record begins with a 32 bit command tag and a 32 bit speed. Next come single byte link attributes for duplex, port kind, PHY address, autonegotiation and MDIO support, followed by separate bytes for crossover status and control. A signed byte then gives the number of 32 bit words used for each link mode mask. Further single bytes carry transceiver kind, master slave configuration and state, plus rate matching mode. Seven reserved 32 bit words follow. Outside the kernel an additional trailing flexible array holds three consecutive mask groups for local support, local advertisement and peer advertisement, each sized by the word count.
PHY attachment direction is a two value enumeration with zero for MAC attached and one for PHY attached, distinguishing whether the PHY sits directly beneath the MAC or beneath another PHY.

The generic netlink family uses the name ethtool with version one. UDP tunnel classification uses values zero one and two for VXLAN, GENEVE and VXLAN GPE, with a private count and a maximum defined as count minus one.

Request headers carry flag bits where compact bitsets is one, omit reply is two and statistics is four. TCP data split is a three state enumeration for unknown disabled and enabled in order. Hardware timestamp source is one for network device and two for PHY library. Power sourcing fault events use values 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64 for over current, over temperature, detection, classification, disconnection, over budget and software power control error, where the middle three detection classification and disconnection names use a C33 scoped prefix.

Netlink attributes for each operation follow a common shape with a zero valued unspecified entry, a sequence of named fields, a private count and a maximum equal to count minus one. This pattern repeats for headers, bitsets, strings, string sets, private flags, rings, MAC merge, link info, link modes, link state, debug, wake, features, channels, interrupt moderation, profiles, coalescing, pause and energy efficient Ethernet. Counts only and nested bitset value mask triples appear where the operation needs them.

Several sentinels share patterns across unrelated fields and must not be confused. All bits set appears as unknown duplex, other port, no change transform and any classifier location in different widths, while top bit set appears both as generic flow extension and as classifier special flag. Near maximal all ones values encode drop versus wake cookies and any first last locations that differ by only one or two. The negative one speed sentinel arrives wrapped as a large unsigned value, the IP user flow alias duplicates the version four user value, and the secured magic bit depends on the plain magic bit.

Two small inline helpers serve as the only executable entry points in the visible range: one checks a 32 bit speed word against the signed limit and unknown sentinel, the other checks an 8 bit duplex byte against the three legal codes. Both are pure predicates with no locking, allocation or I/O.
